events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.90)
events.body:
The driver cancelled and claims rider no-show, so the case enters through NS-0 [F4], whose rider-no-show branch is NS-1. Two of the three NS-1 conditions are met: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 13:02:35 with GPS showing 39 m from the pickup [F6], satisfying NS-1 (i) and (ii) (the 200 m radius is the data-layer parameter; closest approach overall was 38 m [F1]), and the trace records no GPS hole covering the wait [F2][F6].

The third condition fails. NS-1 (iii) requires continuous waiting at the pickup for more than 3 minutes after the arrival confirmation until cancellation. The driver's tap was at 13:02:35 and the cancellation at 13:05:30 [F6][F4], giving only 175 s (2 min 55 s) inside the radius — short of the 180 s threshold [F6]. The earlier period within 200 m (from 13:01:00, 4 min 30 s cumulative [F2], including 3 min 15 s stationary from 13:02:15 [F3]) does not count: NS-1 counts only from the arrival confirmation, and the platform's 13:01:00 arrival record [F5] is not the driver's tap. So the fee was not earned.

Because NS-1 (iii) fails, NS-2 applies: the $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded in full [F4][F7]. I am not applying the NS-2 flag, because the trace settles that the arrival confirmation was made while the driver was at the pickup (39 m [F6]) and no fake confirmation is recorded — the shortfall is one of duration, not of location. The profile facts (driver with 1 upheld no-show dispute in 90 d [F17], rider with none [F16]) do not decide this case and RD-6 is not triggered (no RD-2 refund, and it is a routing clause). The refund follows NS-7: a voucher, not cash.

Safety screen: I read both chat messages and the driver's written statement. Chat #2 "More than 3 min already, I have to cancel" [F10] and the statement "No rider, so I cancelled" [F12] are ordinary no-show handling; Chat #1 is a pickup arrangement [F9]. No threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation appears in the complaint, chat or statement, so the screen is none [F9][F10][F12].

Evidence is sufficient: the arrival tap, its GPS distance, the continuous in-radius duration and the cancellation time are all on record and timestamped [F1][F2][F3][F4][F5][F6][F7][F11], so the single disputed element — the length of the wait — is settled against the fee by the trace's own timing.

No action is being taken on your account. If you're waiting on a rider, it's worth holding past the 3-minute mark before cancelling.
